CLOSING ON VERIFIED COMPLETION. This bead has been P1 OPEN all evening while every slice under it
was finished. I measured rather than trusting its own status note, which was written at 15:35Z and
had been wrong for nine hours.

ALL TEN TYPES, read from the source just now:
  final class TranscriptAtlas private (        core/transcript.scala:81
  final class SurfaceAtlas private (           core/atlas.scala:160
  final class LatePoolingRecipe private (      embed-core/identity.scala:190
  final class SidecarManifest private (        features/sidecar.scala:45
  final class FeatureRef private (             features/sidecar.scala:127
  final class FeatureDerivation private (      features/derivation.scala:148
  final class InterviewSource private (        interview/atlas.scala:33
  final class RecallGraph[S <: RecallGraphStatus] private (  recall/graph.scala:26
  final class PromptPackageManifest private (  acquire/prompt.scala:55
  final class Gold private (                   embed-bench/gold.scala:76
Control still holds: ClaimMeta is `final class ClaimMeta private (` at core/claim.scala:46, so the
screen still discriminates rather than flagging everything.

NOT JUST PRIVATISED -- GUARDED. Each type is named in at least one compile-time probe suite, and I
verified the assertions are real rather than counting mentions. Sample, acquireprobe:
  test("PromptPackageManifest has no derived fromProduct bypass")
  test("PromptPackageManifest has no copy door")
probed from OUTSIDE storymodel4s.acquire, asserting errors.nonEmpty. So a regression is a failing
test, not a silent reopening.

ALL SIX CHILD BEADS CLOSED: slices A, B, C, D1, D2 and the RecallGraph bead. The last status note
here recorded C and D1 as "reserved, no operation since 15:06", D2 as sequenced-after-E, and E as
"BLOCKED twice over". Every one of those completed and nobody came back to the parent.

AND THIS IS THE THIRD VENUE TONIGHT FOR THE SAME ROT, which is why I am writing it up rather than
just closing:
  THE CANDIDATE LEDGER -- two of three `pending blocked` candidates were already on main.
  THE WORKTREES -- 17 of 23 held work that is already an ancestor of main.
  THE BEAD BOARD -- this P1, every child closed, every type fixed.

THE GENERAL FORM: A STATUS RECORD THAT IS WRITTEN ONCE AND NEVER RE-DERIVED ROTS, AND THE ROT
ALWAYS POINTS THE SAME WAY -- toward reporting FINISHED work as OUTSTANDING. It is not symmetric,
and the asymmetry has a cause: these records are updated on CREATION and on FAILURE, because those
are the moments someone is motivated to write. Completion is the moment everyone walks away. So
every such record drifts toward a backlog of ghosts, and the cost is not untidiness -- it is people
being assigned work that is already done, which is exactly what nearly happened here with a P1.

THE COUNTERMEASURE IS THE SAME IN ALL THREE: DO NOT READ THE STATUS, DERIVE IT. Ancestry for
candidates and worktrees (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`); the source itself for a code finding;
child status for a parent bead. Every check above took under a minute and each one contradicted a
record.

Nobody did anything wrong here. Six people finished six slices correctly and none of them owned the
parent. That is a structural gap, not a lapse, and it is mine -- I own this bead board.
